description: AstroGuard AI is an intelligent astronaut health monitoring and anomaly detection system that integrates real-time physiological data, personalized health baselines, spacecraft environmental monitoring, and NASA medical research to identify health risks, provide early warnings, and support autonomous medical decision-making during space missions.
summary: AstroGuard AI is an autonomous astronaut health monitoring and detection system designed to improve crew safety during space missions. It integrates physiological measurements, wearable devices, spacecraft environmental data, and NASA medical research to identify potential health risks. Combining personalized health references, rule-based detection, and local artificial intelligence, AstroGuard provides explainable alerts, recommended actions, and medical handover reports. Using Inspiration4 research as a historical demonstration, AstroGuard illustrates how scientific evidence can support intelligent health monitoring system.
details:
AstroGuard is an AI-powered health monitoring system designed to help astronauts stay safe during space missions. Our goal is to detect potential health problems early, rather than simply record health data.

The system allows astronauts to enter health measurements, connect wearable devices, and complete cognitive tests. It analyzes information such as heart rate, blood pressure, blood oxygen, and radiation exposure to identify potential risks and recommend next steps. We also created an interactive body map to make health information easier to understand.

Our project uses NASA research and Inspiration4 mission data to demonstrate how AstroGuard could work during real space missions. One of our most important features is offline operation, which allows astronauts to receive health guidance even when communication with Earth is limited.

We used HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Python, Visual Studio Code, GitHub, and Qwen3 AI to develop our project.

What makes AstroGuard creative is how it combines real space research, artificial intelligence, and interactive health monitoring into one platform. During development, we considered medical safety, data accuracy, privacy, individual health differences, and ease of use.

Although AstroGuard is currently a prototype, we hope it can contribute to safer space exploration and help astronauts become more independent during future missions to the Moon and Mars.
